result:
Your best leads are people who already know you: shop customers and current subscribers. With €300 a month, spend on things that turn those people into subscribers. Wide advertising will cost more per signup. In order of payoff:

## 1. Sell the box at the counter
Walk-in customers already like your bread and live nearby, so they're the easiest to convert.
- Put a sign at the till and a sample box on display.
- Offer a **first box at half price**, but only for people who sign up in the shop or with a QR code there.
- Have whoever is at the till mention it to regulars. Getting 3–5 signups a week this way would be a good result.

## 2. Referrals from your 140 subscribers
- **Give one box, get one box:** the new subscriber gets their first box free, and the person who referred them gets a free box too. It only costs you ingredients and labour, not €18 in cash.
- Put a referral card in every Saturday box, and update the offer each month.

## 3. Christmas gift subscriptions (start this week)
It's mid-November, so this is the most timely idea on the list.
- Sell **4-week and 8-week gift boxes** with a nice printed card, both in the shop and online.
- Gift recipients get to try the box without any decision to make, and many will keep paying afterwards. Ask them if they want to continue in week 3.

## 4. Get more subscribers on streets you already deliver to
Each new subscriber on an existing route costs almost nothing extra to deliver.
- Put leaflets through doors on the streets your bike already passes (about €60–80 for printing).
- The cargo bike is free advertising, so make sure it has clear branding and your URL or QR code.
- Ask local cafés, coworking spaces, nurseries and gyms within 3 km to display a flyer or host a tasting. An office ordering a box for the team on Friday or Saturday could be a good B2B add-on.

## 5. Keep the subscribers you have
Losing fewer subscribers grows your numbers as surely as gaining new ones.
- Make **pausing easy** (holidays, travel) so people don't cancel.
- Ask everyone who cancels for one reason, and fix the most common one.

## Suggested €300/month split
| Item | € |
|---|---|
| Referral and first-box discounts (ingredient cost) | ~120 |
| Leaflets, referral cards, gift cards | ~80 |
| Tasting events or partner samples | ~60 |
| Small boosted local social posts (Christmas gifts only) | ~40 |

## Two things to check first
1. **Capacity:** how many more boxes can 3 people bake and deliver on a Saturday morning? If the limit is about 180, that's your target, and you may need a waitlist or a second delivery slot before you push harder.
2. **Tracking:** ask every new subscriber how they heard about you. After 6–8 weeks, put more money into whatever is working and stop what isn't.

If you share your weekly signups and cancellations, I can work out which of these will matter most for you.
